title: World Cup Nations Angered by Corporate Box Fees
text: World Cup Nations Angered by Corporate Box Fees Officials from cash-strapped nations are unhappy about paying up to $30,000 for corporate boxes at their own Rugby League World Cup games. ARL Commission chairman Peter V'landys defended the tournament's financial terms. Officials from several cash-strapped nations at the Rugby League World Cup are angry that they must pay tens of thousands of dollars for corporate boxes at their own games to the Australian Rugby League Commission, the tournament organiser. ARL Commission executive chairman Peter V'landys has hosted guests in plush facilities at the Kangaroos' two matches to date, against the Kiwis at Allianz Stadium and against Fiji at Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium last Sunday. But governing bodies from other nations have been forced to dip into limited funds to pay for corporate suites to entertain their VIPs and sponsors when their teams play, rather than having them provided by the World Cup hosts.PNG Considered Abandoning Games Over Box PolicyAccording to sources with knowledge of the issue, speaking on condition of anonymity, Papua New Guinea officials even considered abandoning hosting games during the World Cup if boxes were not made available. In the end, the policy was relaxed for PNG. The men's national team, the Kumuls, and women's side, the Orchids, have since played two World Cup games each in Port Moresby.Other nations, however, have had to stump up as much as $30,000 to the ARL Commission for corporate facilities. That is a departure from the Pacific Championships, where boxes and suites have been supplied to participating countries. One national official said: It's been an absolute joke. Competing nations are also unhappy about the gulf between the treatment of their players and the Australian team.There is a long-standing disparity in player remuneration. Members of Kevin Walters' squad will receive $40,000 for the World Cup, while players from other countries will earn only $850 per game. The Australian fees are dictated by the Rugby League Players' Association's collective bargaining agreement with the ARL Commission.Player Remuneration Gap Sparks Dispute Among NationsOfficials at the World Cup are also annoyed that their players have to share twin rooms at rundown hotels and at times sleep in single beds, while the Australians are put up in their own rooms at top-end lodgings. On Friday, V'landys defended the planning for the tournament, pointing to the funds provided to competing nations. Every nation executes a participation agreement. Accordingly, we pay each nation a participation payment, he said.In addition, we make payments to the players, pay for flights, accommodation, travel and meals for 32 players and officials per team. We also provide 112 complimentary admission tickets and prize money of $475,000 each for the men's and women's World Cups. We invite travelling administrators into the official ARLC function. As you can see, we cover nearly all costs and pay them to participate.They signed an agreement and knew of the terms. It is disappointing they cherry-pick; as you can see, they receive a very good deal. V'landys said the pre-tournament complication with PNG emerged because administrators there mistakenly believed they were a host nation and had committed to providing boxes they were not entitled to. We helped them out by giving up the ARLC box and other boxes to cover their mistake, he said.Vlandys Defends Treatment Of Competing Nations TeamsWe acted in good faith as they made a mistake and were never threatened about them pulling out. Another source of displeasure among some officials is suggestions that Australia and New Zealand will get first choice of hotels for the semi-finals in Sydney and Newcastle. That is despite the fact the Kiwis will finish second in Pool A in the men's tournament following a 24-22 defeat to the Kangaroos on October 15.The reward for winning Pool B, meanwhile, is a six-day turnaround in a secondary hotel in Newcastle. National teams are wary about airing their frustrations publicly, considering the importance of Australia to international competition and the comparative commercial might of the ARL Commission, which owns the NRL.IRL Plans To Run Future World Cups DirectlyHowever, the experience of this World Cup could shape decision-making regarding the next one. Sources say the International Rugby League will no longer sell rights to the World Cup to a host country or countries. Instead, the IRL plans to run future editions itself, possibly in partnership with the ARL Commission. Under one scenario to be discussed at an IRL board meeting next week, the ARL Commission would jointly underwrite the 2030 World Cup despite Australia not physically hosting it.The location of the tournament is set to be announced next month. Recent developments have helped convince the international federation, on whose board V'landys sits, to go in the new direction. The IRL is in dispute with England's Rugby Football League over $800,000 in allegedly outstanding payments from the 2022 World Cup. The original host of this year's tournament, France, withdrew for financial reasons, leading Australia to step in.Australia's staging of the Rugby League World Cup has been a raging success on the surface, drawing strong crowds and television ratings and already featuring an epic showdown between the Kangaroos and New Zealand.
summary: But governing bodies from other nations have been forced to dip into limited funds to pay for corporate suites to entertain their VIPs and sponsors when their teams play, rather than having them provided by the World Cup hosts.PNG Considered Abandoning Games Over Box PolicyAccording to sources with knowledge of the issue, speaking on condition of anonymity, Papua New Guinea officials even considered abandoning hosting games during the World Cup if boxes were not made available.
